newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket launches double satellite payload.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket launches double satellite payload.

text.p: Western Europe's 97th Ariane rocket blasted off from French Guiana on Tuesday carrying two telecommunications satellites.
The Ariane-4 rocket lifted off at 8.20 p.m. (2320 GMT) from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch center in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.

The INMARSAT-3F4 satellite separated from the Ariane rocket 21 minutes later, space officials said. INMARSAT-3F4 will provide mobile telecommunications in the western Atlantic ocean region for the London-based International Maritime Satellite Organisation (INMARSAT).
The satellite was built in the U.S. by Lockheed Martin.

Five minutes later, the INSAT-2D satellite, built in India by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) separated from the rocket. It will provide telecommunications throughout India and neigbouring countries.
Tuesday's launch was the fourth of 12 Ariane rocket launches planned for this year by the Paris-based Arianespace company.
